name: 6 x 6 mm tactile switch (through-hole, 4 legs)
blurb: Small push button that connects two points while pressed; the four legs are really two electrical connections.

pins.note: Legs 1 and 1b are connected inside the switch. Use either one.
Legs 2 and 2b are connected inside the switch. Pressing the button joins node 1 to node 2.

search: 6x6mm tactile push button switch THT 4 pin

verify: Overall height 5.0 mm matches the Omron B3F-1020 style; the very common 4.3 mm (B3F-1000), 7.3 mm (B3F-1050) and other heights exist, so measure the overall height of the switch you have with calipers and edit maxHeight and the cap height. Confirmed by the Omron B3F drawing and the KiCad footprint (two independent sources): 6 x 6 mm body, leg pitch 6.5 mm by 4.5 mm (the earlier 6.25 mm was wrong), 3.5 mm plunger, body about 3.4 mm high. Legs 6.5 mm apart (same y) are the same node in the KiCad footprint; confirm with a continuity meter. The 6.5 mm wide body here is the 6 mm housing plus the leg overhang. Clone switches are not held to Omron tolerances (+-0.2 on the body, +-0.1 on the hole pitch): test fit before printing a tight lid opening. Peak current is the Omron 50 mA at 24 V DC contact rating, not a measurement. Drawing-only fields on the pins: z -3.4 puts each leg at the foot of the 3.4 mm body, where the legs leave it; lead 3.5 mm is a typical leg length for this switch and was not read from the drawing.
sources: https://media.onlinecomponents.com/productfiles/mf-om/d22b3f0401.pdf (Omron B3F catalogue, opened and read: body 6 +-0.2 x 6 +-0.2, PCB holes 6.5 +-0.1 x 4.5 +-0.1 at 1 mm dia, plunger 3.5 mm dia, body 3.4, B3F-1000 total 4.3 +-0.2, B3F-1020 5 +0.05/-0.2, B3F-1050 7.3 +-0.2, 50 mA 24 V DC rating)

https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints/-/raw/master/Button_Switch_THT.pretty/SW_PUSH_6mm.kicad_mod (KiCad library, opened: pads at 0 and 6.5 mm by 0 and 4.5 mm, 1.1 mm drill, same pad number 1 or 2 on legs 6.5 mm apart, body 6 x 6 mm)
